P01.title: Close internet entry on Ivanti Connect Secure VPN (vpn-gw-01) that leads to the domain controller
P01.summary: Validated path P01 starts at the internet-facing corporate VPN, vpn-gw-01 (Ivanti Connect Secure), where CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 together gave the validation agent an authenticated shell on the appliance. Admin credentials cached on vpn-gw-01 also worked on the IT admin jump host jump-it-01, and the jump host admin group has RDP rights on the domain controller dc-01, where the agent opened a read-only RDP session. Fixing vpn-gw-01 breaks the path at its first step.
P01.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take over the corporate VPN, reuse its admin credentials on the IT jump host, and log on to the domain controller. Control of the domain controller would let them reach nearly every corporate account and system, opening the door to ransomware and to staging attacks toward operational networks. These two flaws are among the most widely exploited and are used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, block the management interface of the Ivanti Connect Secure appliance vpn-gw-01 from the internet and limit its web interfaces to known source addresses where remote access needs allow it.

Apply the fixed release and mitigations from the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 on vpn-gw-01, and run its integrity-check steps; if no mitigation can be applied, take vpn-gw-01 out of service until one can.
Check vpn-gw-01 for signs of compromise, including unexpected files, accounts or configuration changes, and end all active VPN and admin sessions on it.

Reset every admin credential cached on vpn-gw-01, and with the Windows Server team reset the same credentials where they are reused on jump-it-01 so no account is shared between the appliance and the jump host.
verify_steps: Confirm from an outside network that the vpn-gw-01 management interface is unreachable and that the appliance reports the fixed release with a clean integrity check.
Confirm the old admin credentials from vpn-gw-01 no longer authenticate on vpn-gw-01 or jump-it-01.
Ask the validation team to rerun path P01 and confirm it no longer gets past vpn-gw-01.
P01.exec_line: Our corporate VPN has two actively exploited flaws that let outsiders reach the domain controller; Network Engineering is patching it now.
P01.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P02.title: Close internet entry point on field office VPN gateway vpn-gw-02 (Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN) leading to the domain controller
P02.summary: Validated path P02 starts at vpn-gw-02, the Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN used by field offices, where CVE-2024-21762 gave an unauthenticated foothold from the internet. From there the print spooler flaw CVE-2021-34527 on file server fs-02 gave SYSTEM rights. A cached domain admin logon found on fs-02 was then usable against domain controller dc-01. Fixing vpn-gw-02 breaks the path at its first step.
P02.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could go from the internet to full control of Active Directory, which means control of user accounts, servers and the ability to spread anywhere on the corporate network. For the utility that could mean a ransomware outage of business systems and a launch point toward operational networks. Both flaws on this path are widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, limit exposure of the SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02: block its management interface from the internet and restrict SSL-VPN access to known field office address ranges, or disable SSL-VPN until patched if that is not possible.

Upgrade Fortinet FortiOS on vpn-gw-02 to the fixed release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-21762; if no fix or mitigation is available, take the gateway out of service.
Check vpn-gw-02 for signs of compromise: review configuration for unknown accounts or changes and review logs for unexpected logins or traffic since the flaw became known.
End all active VPN sessions and reset the credentials of local admin accounts and VPN user accounts on vpn-gw-02.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-02 reports the fixed FortiOS release from the vendor's advisory and that its management interface is not reachable from the internet.
Confirm only expected admin and VPN accounts exist on vpn-gw-02 and that their credentials were reset after the upgrade.
Request a rerun of the validation of path P02 to confirm it no longer succeeds.
P02.exec_line: A known flaw in our field office remote access gateway could let outsiders take over our core user directory; patching now closes it.
P02.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P03.title: Patch Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 to close the contractor-gateway path to the email server
P03.summary: The validation tool confirmed path P03. Session tokens leaked by the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 (contractor gateway, internet zone) through CVE-2023-4966 let a contractor session be taken over. From that session, the Microsoft Exchange Server on exch-01 (email server, corporate zone) answered a server-side request forgery check for CVE-2022-41040. Fixing nsg-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path. exch-01 should still be patched separately by Messaging.
P03.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could hijack a contractor's gateway session without a password and reach the corporate email server. From there they could read or tamper with utility email and use it as a foothold for wider intrusion, including ransomware, which both flaws are known to be used for. Both are among the most widely exploited flaws seen today.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 so only known contractor sources can reach it, and block its management interface from the internet.
Upgrade the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 to the fixed release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-4966.
After the upgrade, end all active and persistent sessions on nsg-01 so any stolen session tokens stop working.
Check nsg-01 and the contractor sessions it served for signs of compromise, including unexpected logins, session reuse from unfamiliar addresses, and new accounts or configuration changes.
Reset the credentials of the contractor accounts that used nsg-01, starting with the account whose session was taken over in this validation.
verify_steps: Confirm nsg-01 reports the fixed release and that its management interface cannot be reached from the internet.
Confirm that sessions created before the upgrade are no longer accepted by nsg-01.
Ask the validation team to rerun path P03 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P03.exec_line: A flaw in our contractor remote access gateway could let outsiders reach the company email server; patching the gateway closes it.
P03.route_reason: The path ends at exch-01, the email server, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes straight to Network Engineering.

P04.title: Patch PAN-OS GlobalProtect on plant edge firewall fw-edge-03 (CVE-2024-3400) and end password reuse with OT jump host
P04.summary: Validated path P04 runs from the internet to the plant data historian. The GlobalProtect portal on plant edge firewall fw-edge-03 (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS) is exploitable through CVE-2024-3400, which was confirmed. The firewall's management account password is the same as the local admin password on the IT to OT jump host ot-jump-01, and the historian hist-01 accepts logons from that jump host. The validation agent stopped at the OT boundary and did not log on to ot-jump-01 or hist-01. Fixing fw-edge-03 breaks the path at its entry point.
P04.why_it_matters: An unauthenticated attacker on the internet could take full control of the plant edge firewall and reuse its management password to log on to the IT to OT jump host and then the plant data historian. That would put an attacker at the boundary of our operational technology network, with access to plant operating data and a foothold toward control systems. This flaw is among the most heavily exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, enable the vendor's Threat Prevention signatures for this vulnerability on the GlobalProtect portal of fw-edge-03 (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS), and make sure the firewall's management interface is not reachable from the internet.
Upgrade PAN-OS on fw-edge-03 to the fixed release named in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-3400, and complete the mitigation and integrity-check steps listed in that advisory.

Check fw-edge-03 for signs of compromise, such as unexpected admin accounts, configuration changes, unknown files or unusual outbound connections, and hand any findings to incident response before continuing.

End all active admin sessions on fw-edge-03 and reset its management account password to a unique value, then work with OT Engineering to change the local admin password on ot-jump-01 so the two no longer match.
verify_steps: Confirm fw-edge-03 is running the fixed PAN-OS release from the vendor's advisory and that the Threat Prevention signatures are active on the GlobalProtect portal.
Have OT Engineering confirm the ot-jump-01 local admin password was changed and no longer matches the fw-edge-03 management account password.
Request a rerun of the validation for attack path P04 to show the path is closed.
P04.exec_line: An internet-facing plant firewall flaw could let attackers reach our plant data historian; patching the firewall and changing a shared password closes it.
P04.route_reason: The path ends at hist-01, the plant data historian, which is marked as a crown jewel, and passes through the crown jewel jump host ot-jump-01.

P05.title: Patch SQL injection in internet-facing Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 (Vendor file exchange)
P05.summary: Validated path P05 shows that the internet-facing Vendor file exchange (mft-01), running Progress MOVEit Transfer, is exposed to CVE-2023-34362, an unauthenticated SQL injection. The validation tool confirmed the flaw with a read of the version table only. This is a single-step path: fixing mft-01 closes it.
P05.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could reach the database behind the vendor file exchange without logging in. They could read, change or delete the files and records the utility swaps with its vendors, which could expose sensitive business or operational data and set up extortion. This flaw has been used heavily in mass data-theft and ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict web access to Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 so only known vendor IP ranges and internal users can reach it, or take it off the internet until patched.
Apply the fixed release of Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01, following the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-34362 for the fixed release and its mitigation and integrity-check steps.

After patching, check mft-01 for signs of compromise: unfamiliar files in the web application folders, unexpected or newly created user or admin accounts, unusual large downloads in transfer logs, and unexpected database changes.

End all active sessions on mft-01 and reset credentials it uses, including MOVEit administrator accounts and the database service account, then tell affected vendors to rotate any credentials stored there.
verify_steps: Confirm the MOVEit Transfer version on mft-01 matches the fixed release named in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-34362.
Confirm from an outside network address that is not on the allowlist that the mft-01 web interface is not reachable, if access was restricted.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of path P05 against mft-01 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P05.exec_line: Our internet-facing vendor file exchange has a widely exploited flaw that could expose shared files; we are restricting access and patching it now.
P05.route_reason: The path ends at mft-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the Enterprise Applications owner team.

P06.title: Close internet-exposed admin setup on Partner wiki (wiki-ext, Confluence Data Center, CVE-2023-22515)
P06.summary: Validated path P06: the Partner wiki (wiki-ext), running Atlassian Confluence Data Center in the internet zone, exposes a setup endpoint affected by CVE-2023-22515 that allows creation of an administrator account. The validation agent confirmed the endpoint was reachable from the internet and stopped before creating an account. Fixing wiki-ext closes this single-step path.
P06.why_it_matters: An outsider could make themselves an administrator of the Partner wiki and read, change or delete everything shared there with partners, including project documents and contact details. That access could also be used to plant malicious content or links aimed at partners and staff, damaging trust and creating a foothold for further attacks. This flaw is widely exploited and has been used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict internet access to the Partner wiki (wiki-ext) so only known partner and staff addresses or a VPN can reach it, and block the setup and administration endpoints from the internet entirely.
Upgrade Atlassian Confluence Data Center on wiki-ext to the fixed release named in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-22515, and apply its listed mitigation and integrity-check steps.

Check wiki-ext for evidence of compromise: review the administrator group and user list for accounts nobody recognizes, recently installed plugins, and unexpected configuration or content changes, and report any positive findings to CISA.
Remove any unauthorized accounts found, end all active sessions, and reset passwords for legitimate administrator accounts on wiki-ext.
verify_steps: From an outside network, confirm the setup and administration endpoints on wiki-ext are no longer reachable.
Confirm in the Confluence administration console that wiki-ext reports the fixed version and that the administrator list contains only approved accounts.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P06 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P06.exec_line: Our partner wiki can be taken over by outsiders through a known, actively exploited flaw; we are restricting access and patching it now.
P06.route_reason: The path ends at wiki-ext, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the Collaboration Tools team.

P07.title: Close unauthenticated setup access on ScreenConnect remote support console rmm-01 to cut path to virtualization cluster esxi-07
P07.summary: Validated path P07 starts at the internet-facing ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote support console (rmm-01), where the setup wizard was reachable without authentication (CVE-2024-1709). From there an attacker can create a directory group that the VMware ESXi virtualization cluster (esxi-07) trusts for admin access (CVE-2024-37085) and take full control of the hypervisors. Fixing rmm-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P07.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could take over the remote support console and use it to gain full control of the virtualization cluster that runs corporate servers. That would let them shut down, encrypt or steal every virtual machine on esxi-07, a pattern that ransomware groups widely use and that could disrupt business operations across the utility.
fix_steps: Today, block internet access to the ConnectWise ScreenConnect management and setup interface on rmm-01 so that only approved internal or VPN addresses can reach it.
Upgrade ScreenConnect on rmm-01 to the fixed release, and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-1709.

Check rmm-01 for compromise: review all ScreenConnect user accounts and remove any administrator accounts that were not created by the IT Service Desk, and review recent sessions and installed extensions for unknown activity.
End all active ScreenConnect sessions on rmm-01 and reset the passwords of all ScreenConnect administrator accounts and any directory service account the console uses.
Notify Infrastructure to confirm that no unexpected directory groups trusted by the esxi-07 hypervisors were created or changed from the console.
verify_steps: From an internet location, confirm the ScreenConnect management and setup interface on rmm-01 cannot be reached.
Confirm in the ScreenConnect admin console that rmm-01 runs the fixed release and that the setup wizard requires authentication or is no longer available.
Request a rerun of the validation of attack path P07 to confirm it no longer succeeds.
P07.exec_line: An internet-facing remote support tool could let attackers seize our virtualization servers; we are locking it down and patching it now.
P07.route_reason: The path ends at esxi-07, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes directly to the IT Service Desk as owner of the fix point rmm-01.

P08.title: Close the internet-exposed Cisco IOS XE web UI on substation router rtr-sub-12 (path P08 to the EMS data link)
P08.summary: The validation tool confirmed that the Cisco IOS XE web UI on rtr-sub-12 (Substation comms router) is reachable from the internet and runs a version affected by CVE-2023-20198. From that router, a route to ems-link-01 (Energy management system data link) exists with no access list between the substation comms network and the EMS data link. No traffic was sent to the EMS link during testing. Fixing rtr-sub-12 breaks the path at its entry point. The missing access list on ems-link-01 is a separate gap for Grid Operations to review.
P08.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could take full control of the substation router and then use it to reach the data link that feeds the energy management system. That could expose grid control data and operations to tampering or disruption. This flaw is among the most widely exploited on the internet.
fix_steps: Today, block the Cisco IOS XE web UI on rtr-sub-12 from the internet and all untrusted networks, or turn the web UI off if Field Telecom does not need it.
Upgrade rtr-sub-12 to the fixed Cisco IOS XE release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-20198.

Check rtr-sub-12 for signs of compromise, including unknown local accounts with full (level 15) privileges and unexpected configuration changes. If you find any, isolate the router and report the finding to CISA immediately.
Remove any unrecognized accounts from rtr-sub-12, end active management sessions, and reset all local administrative credentials on the router.
verify_steps: From an external network, confirm the rtr-sub-12 web UI cannot be reached.
Confirm rtr-sub-12 runs the fixed Cisco IOS XE release and lists only approved local accounts.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P08 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P08.exec_line: An internet-exposed substation router could let attackers reach the energy management system link; we are closing internet access and patching it now.
P08.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P09.title: Patch Apache Log4j2 on internet-facing Outage map API (outage-api) to close remote code execution path P09
P09.summary: The validation tool confirmed that the Outage map API (outage-api), an internet-facing Java service using Apache Log4j2, is vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228. A harmless lookup string sent in a request header caused the service to make an outbound DNS query, showing that untrusted input reaches the vulnerable logging library. This is the only step on the path, so fixing outage-api closes it.
P09.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could run their own code on the server behind the public outage map, giving them a foothold inside the utility's network. From there they could tamper with outage information customers rely on during storms or use the server to move toward other systems. This flaw is widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, reduce exposure of the Outage map API (outage-api): block its outbound internet connections except those it strictly needs, and if it cannot be patched quickly, take it off the internet until it is.

Update Apache Log4j2 in the outage-api Java service to a fixed release, following the vendor's advisory for CVE-2021-44228 for the fixed version and its mitigation and integrity-check steps. Temporary mitigations are acceptable only until the update is in place.
Check outage-api for signs of compromise: review logs and outbound connection records since December 2021 for unexpected lookups, unknown files, new accounts or scheduled tasks.
Reset any credentials, keys or tokens stored on or used by outage-api, and rebuild the host from a known good image if any sign of compromise is found.
verify_steps: Confirm the deployed outage-api build contains only the fixed Apache Log4j2 release, including any copies bundled inside other libraries.
Confirm outage-api's outbound network rules block connections and DNS lookups to destinations it does not need.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P09 against outage-api and confirm no outbound DNS query is triggered.
P09.exec_line: Our public outage map server has a widely exploited flaw letting outsiders take control; we are patching it now.
P09.route_reason: The path ends at outage-api, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the Customer Applications team.

P10.title: Close unauthenticated takeover of FortiManager firewall manager (fmgr-01) from the corporate network
P10.summary: Validation confirmed that the device registration port on the Firewall manager (fmgr-01, Fortinet FortiManager) answers from the corporate user network and runs a version affected by CVE-2024-47575, a missing authentication flaw that lets a remote attacker run code on the manager without logging in. This is a single-step path: reaching fmgr-01 is enough to take it over.
P10.why_it_matters: FortiManager holds the configuration for the firewalls it manages, so an attacker who controls fmgr-01 could change firewall rules, open paths between network zones, or switch off protections across the utility. That could expose operational systems that the firewalls are meant to isolate and would be hard to detect, because the changes would come from a trusted management tool. This flaw is widely exploited in the wild.
fix_steps: Today, restrict the device registration port on the Firewall manager (fmgr-01, Fortinet FortiManager) so it only accepts connections from the addresses of the FortiGate firewalls it manages, and block it from the corporate user network and the internet.
Upgrade fmgr-01 to the fixed FortiManager release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-47575.

Check fmgr-01 for signs of compromise: look for unknown or unexpected registered devices, unexplained configuration changes, and new administrator accounts, and compare pushed firewall policies against a known-good baseline.
After the checks, reset the administrator passwords on fmgr-01 and any credentials it stores for managed firewalls, and end all active administrative sessions.
verify_steps: From a host on the corporate user network, confirm the device registration port on fmgr-01 no longer responds, while managed FortiGate firewalls still connect normally.
Confirm the FortiManager version on fmgr-01 matches the fixed release named in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-47575.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P10 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P10.exec_line: An attacker on our office network could take over the tool that controls our firewalls; we are locking it down and patching.
P10.route_reason: The path ends at fmgr-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the owning team, Network Engineering.

P11.title: Patch Netlogon (Zerologon) on domain controller dc-01 reachable from corporate workstations
P11.summary: Validation confirmed that domain controller dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory) runs a version affected by CVE-2020-1472 and accepts Netlogon secure channel connections from corporate workstations. The agent confirmed the version only and made no change. This single-step path means any compromised corporate workstation could be used to attack the domain controller directly.
P11.why_it_matters: An attacker on any corporate workstation could take over dc-01 and with it control of every account and domain-joined system in Active Directory. That would let them reach business systems, push ransomware across the domain, and potentially pivot toward operational networks that rely on corporate identity. This flaw is widely exploited and has known use in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, limit network access to Netlogon and RPC services on dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory) to only the domain-joined systems and subnets that need it, and alert on unexpected Netlogon secure channel connections to dc-01.
Apply the fixed update to dc-01 and complete the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2020-1472, coordinating with any other domain controllers in the same domain.

After patching, check dc-01 for signs of compromise: review security logs for unexpected changes to the domain controller's computer account password, new or modified privileged accounts, and unusual replication or logon activity.
If any sign of compromise is found, escalate to incident response and reset the dc-01 computer account and privileged domain credentials before returning to normal operations.
verify_steps: Confirm dc-01 reports the fixed update as installed and that its Windows Server version is no longer in the affected range for CVE-2020-1472.

Confirm security logs on dc-01 show Netlogon secure channel connections are only accepted in the protected form described in the vendor's advisory, and that no denied or vulnerable connection events remain unexplained.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P11 against dc-01 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P11.exec_line: Our main domain controller has a widely exploited flaw letting any office computer seize control of all company accounts; patching urgently.
P11.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, which is marked as a crown jewel asset, so the ticket requires human review before assignment.

P12.title: Restrict RDP to OT jump host ot-jump-01 and require MFA to close corporate path to EMS data link
P12.summary: Validation confirmed that the IT to OT jump host ot-jump-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, OT DMZ) shows a password-only RDP logon prompt to the whole corporate network, including a corporate desktop VLAN, with no multi-factor prompt. The Energy management system data link ems-link-01 trusts logons coming from ot-jump-01, so anyone who signs in to the jump host could reach the EMS data link. The agent reached the logon prompt but did not attempt a logon. Fixing RDP access on ot-jump-01 breaks the path.
P12.why_it_matters: Anyone on the corporate network who guesses or steals a password could sign in to the OT jump host and from there reach the energy management system data link. That link feeds grid operations, so an intruder could disrupt or tamper with data operators rely on to run the grid. Both assets are crown jewels in the OT DMZ.
fix_steps: On ot-jump-01 (Microsoft Windows Server), restrict inbound RDP at the firewall today so only a named group of approved administrator workstations or a privileged access subnet can reach it, and block it from the general corporate network and desktop VLANs.
Require multi-factor authentication for every RDP logon to ot-jump-01, for example through an MFA-enforcing remote access gateway in front of the host, and remove password-only sign-in.
Limit who may log on to ot-jump-01 over RDP to a small, reviewed list of named OT Engineering accounts and remove any shared or unused accounts.
Review ot-jump-01 logon history for unexpected RDP sign-ins from corporate network addresses, and if any are found, reset the affected account passwords and escalate to the incident response team.
verify_steps: From a corporate desktop VLAN, confirm the RDP service on ot-jump-01 can no longer be reached.
From an approved administrator workstation, confirm an RDP logon to ot-jump-01 requires a multi-factor prompt and fails with a password alone.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of path P12 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P12.exec_line: Our corporate network can reach the grid control jump server with only a password; we are locking it down and adding multi-factor sign-in.
P12.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel, and the fix point ot-jump-01 is also a crown jewel.
